# Semantic-turn numerical oracles

These are full row-major little-endian f32 arrays, shape `[1, 80, 800]`, generated by the primary
Transformers 4.57.1 `WhisperFeatureExtractor(chunk_length=8)` NumPy CPU implementation, with NumPy
2.2.6. Crop to the last 128000 samples, left-pad to that length, then call with `sampling_rate=16000`,
`padding="max_length"`, `max_length=128000`, `truncation=True`, `do_normalize=True`.

Inputs are defined independently by the Rust tests:

- `short`: repeat 200 times `[0,.25,.5,.75,1,.75,.5,.25,0,-.25,-.5,-.75,-1,-.75,-.5,-.25]`.
- `noise`: 128321 samples, unsigned 32-bit LCG seeded at 17, next state
  `(state * 1664525 + 1013904223) mod 2^32`; f32 sample `(state >> 8) / 8388608 - 1`.
- `speech`: existing `../speech.wav`, signed i16 samples divided by 32768 in f32.
- `silence`: empty input padded to eight seconds; all features are exactly `-1.5`, so no binary
  array is stored for this case.

`reference.json` records feature hashes and probabilities from the pinned v3.0 graph through Python
ONNX Runtime 1.31.0 CPU, one intra/inter-op thread, graph optimization `ORT_ENABLE_ALL`. Rust uses the
same qualified native runtime/settings. An older runtime produced a different probability despite
identical features; these scores are version-specific numerical oracles, not endpoint-quality labels.
Do not weaken tolerances or replace fixtures with Rust-produced results.

[Artifact pins, licenses and native qualification](../../../../../docs/reference/semantic-turn-model.md).
